doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: What angers him and Miles's ability to read people
summary: Being taken advantage of; New York toughness, and Miles's instincts and ease across circles.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Is there anything these days that makes you angry?

Well you get upset when somebody tried to take advantage of you. You get upset about that. So you just have to — but that’s one thing about living in New York — that song is true, if you can make it there you can make it anywhere. So you know you get used to all the con games and all this slicksters and so, a lot of the time you can see things coming. And that was the beauty — when I worked with Miles I enjoyed just hanging out with Miles. Because I knew he was a musical genius, you didn’t even have to think about that. But what impressed me with Miles was I mean he could just see things coming. I mean he would see somebody walking toward him and I know they’re going to ask me to sniff it. And I mean he just knew people and he knew, and that record, “On the Corner” he © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

could go and hang with the guys “On the Corner” and they would be happy and then he would go hang with the guys who played classical music, they would be happy. Everywhere he went, the actresses and dancers, they all were crazy about him. So I mean that’s the one thing I like about Miles, how can he just go from one — I’ll say “genre” — to another or one group, and he’ll still be Miles. So that’s amazing.
